subject: Nordwell Bank — request: 2yr retention for transaction debug traces (SIG/CAIQ evidence)
messages:
From: Anna Petrov <security@nordwellbank.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: Luca Romano <legal@nordwellbank.com>, platformops@nordwellbank.com
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 09:14:00 +0100
Subject: Request: 2-year retention for transaction debug traces / SIG question follow-up

Hi Markus,

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. As part of our vendor assessment (SIG + CAIQ), our legal and investigations teams have requested that Redwood retain a narrow class of "transaction debug traces" for two years. The ask is scoped to records that capture per-transaction debug metadata necessary to reconstruct order-of-operations for disputed transactions (IP address, non-sensitive routing context, anonymized request hashes, and server-side debug IDs).

We understand Redwood's default tenant debug TTL is 90 days per SOC2-aligned policy. Nordwell's regulator requires for certain payment reconciliation investigations a 2-year lookback for debug traces tied to settlement events. We are trying to avoid a full-platform long-retention carveout. Can you confirm:

- Whether Redwood can provide a customer-scoped retention exception limited to a logical log class ("transaction-debug-traces") and not extend TTL for other telemetry?
- What pseudonymization/prefix-redaction options are available so that PII is not stored longer than 90 days?
- Evidence deliverables we can attach to our SIG/CAIQ — ideally a signed statement and a sample manifest of retained artifacts.

Attached: Nordwell_SIG_Q_3-5-2_request.pdf (highlighted fields).

Best,
Anna Petrov
Head of Third-Party Security
Nordwell Bank

From: markus_klein@redwood.ai <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Petrov <security@nordwellbank.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 11:02:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: Request: 2-year retention for transaction debug traces / SIG question follow-up

Anna — thanks for the clear note and the attachment. Internal folks looped in. Quick summary of options from our side and open asks below.

What we can do today
- Customer-scoped TTL exemption: Yes — we support per-tenant retention policies for log classes. We can scope to a named artifact type (we call them "transaction-debug-traces") and set TTL independently.
- Pseudonymization: We can apply deterministic hashing to request identifiers and drop user-identifying payloads before moving traces into the long-retention store. We will not retain raw user content beyond 90 days unless explicitly requested and agreed.
- Evidence: We can produce a signed attestation, a manifest template showing fields retained, and a CAIQ/SIG mapping doc referencing the exception.

Open questions for Nordwell (need answers to scope the work)
1) Are you asking for all transaction debug traces tied to settlement events across all environments (prod only)?
2) Do you require the ability to export raw traces on demand for regulatory requests, or is a sanitized manifest sufficient?
3) Who will sign the legal authorization for an exception — a security POC is fine for engineering but legal needs to sign the MAP addendum.

Internal action items (Kimberly / Neha / Rishi)
- Kimberly: review whether a 2yr exception changes our SOC2 control statements or requires disclosure in a CAIQ.
- Neha: review encryption-at-rest/key scoping for the long-retention bucket and note any KMS changes.
- Rishi: quick check on legal hold language and a suggested MAP addendum.

I'll draft the MAP addendum once we confirm the scope. If Nordwell can confirm 1-3 above this week we can scope engineering work and an ETA for the artifact pack.

Thanks — Markus
Markus Klein
Enterprise Solutions — Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 09:29:00 +01:00
Subject: RE: Request: 2-year retention for transaction debug traces / SIG question follow-up

Markus — thanks for the heads-up. My initial compliance read:

- SOC2 scope: A tenant-specific retention exception for a narrow class is feasible, but we must add a disclosure to our CAIQ/ISO questionnaire that an exception exists and the condition under which it is used. We should avoid changing our global control narrative.
- SIG mapping: we'll map the exception to SIG control "Data Retention" and supply a control narrative and sample manifest (pattern we use for escrow/forensic exports).
- Evidence: I'll prepare a short attestation and a CAIQ appendix that cites the compensated control (pseudonymization + encrypted long-retention store + legal authorization).

Questions for engineering/security (Neha)
- Can the hash-salt be customer-specific and rotated independently? If not, advise mitigation.
- Can we produce an export workflow that redacts PII and includes a chain-of-custody log?

Assuming positive answers, compliance can sign off on the attestation. I'll draft language for the MAP addendum and attach it to the DocuSign link.

—Kimberly Park
Compliance Manager — Redwood Inference

From: Anna Petrov <security@nordwellbank.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: Luca Romano <legal@nordwellbank.com>, platformops@nordwellbank.com
Date: Tue, 17 Feb 2026 15:02:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: Request: 2-year retention for transaction debug traces / SIG question follow-up

Markus / Kimberly / Neha / Rishi — thank you, that all sounds promising. Answers below to your open items:  

1) Scope: Prod-only, only traces tied to settlement events (we will provide a list of event codes). No dev/staging.
2) Export: We require the ability to request an export of raw traces for a regulatory investigation. Exports will be subject to legal authorization (we will sign the MAP addendum). For routine audits a sanitized manifest is acceptable, but for subpoenas/regulatory orders we need raw data.
3) Legal authorization: Our legal lead (Luca) will sign the MAP addendum.

We prefer customer-specific hash-salts and an auditable chain-of-custody for exports. Please indicate estimated timelines for: addendum draft (compliance/legal review), security KMS changes, and engineering build for retention + export workflow. Also: attach the sample manifest you mentioned so we can validate fields against our requirements.

I'll review the CAIQ appendix once you send it.

Best,
Anna
